title: Trace delegate invocation and captured state, including lifetime and multicast failure behavior

rubric.point: Explains lifetime: the captured local `n` does not end when `Make` returns. It is kept in closure state that lives as long as a delegate still references it.
Explains sharing: both lambdas capture the same variable `n`, not separate copies or a snapshot of its value. The increments made through `inc` change the storage that `read` reads.

questions.model: `n` is a captured variable, so it is stored in closure state rather than only in `Make`'s stack frame. That state stays alive after `Make` returns because the delegates still reference it. Both lambdas capture that one variable, not copies of its value. Each `inc()` updates the shared storage, so `read()` sees both increments and returns `2`.
